Variants.Content: Irontree Fort is located deep in the northern woodlands and is often called Irontree Fort. What it symbolizes is another kind of power in the northern forest territory: not gold mines and great harbors, but wood for heating, building houses, building bridges, making spears, and people who have known the forest roads for generations. This place forms a network with surrounding families, logging camps, hunters and small settlements. If any lord ignores these relationships, it will be difficult to truly dominate the forest. The woodland in the north provides resources in peacetime, but in times of war, it obscures the movement, slows down the march, and cuts the news into fragments.

Entry Ironrath Local families also rely on firewood, hunting grounds, peat, salt fish, and granaries to survive the long winter; if any road, well, spring, or wharf fails, the price will fall on them first.

Entry Ironrath They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the North; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hoof.

Entry Ironrath If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Those who repair Irontree Castle are familiar with the stone walls, wooden beams, iron doors, tombs and seams left by generations of repairs. Those who comfort the families of the deceased are familiar with the old gods, weirwood trees and the cemeteries left by their ancestors. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Ironrath They care about firewood, hunting grounds, peat, salt fish, and granaries that can survive the long winter. They also care about whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, they see whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
